dedupe_keys.name: rooftop photovoltaic technical potential in the united states nrel 2016 assessment data

description: This submission holds the data behind NREL's 2016 technical report 'Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Technical Potential in the United States: A Detailed Assessment' by Pieter Gagnon, Robert Margolis and Caleb Phillips: a workbook of rooftop PV technical potential estimates and three sets of shapefiles (ZIP code summaries, small building suitability and raster domains). Buildings are grouped as small (under 5,000 square feet), medium (5,000 to 25,000) and large (over 25,000); roof area counts as suitable when shading allows at least 70 per cent of an unshaded system's output, tilt is at most 60 degrees, the azimuth is not north and at least 10 m2 are contiguous. One tab reports estimates for ZIP codes with some lidar coverage, with the share of each ZIP code covered, and another estimates the number of small buildings and the share with suitable roof area for all ZIP codes in the contiguous US, modelled where lidar was missing. Coverage: contiguous United States. Access: free download (DOI 10.7799/1575064, submitted November 2019, page updated May 2026). Licence: NREL data catalogue terms. Caveats: values for partly covered ZIP codes are under-reported, medium and large buildings were not estimated at ZIP level, and the lidar is now dated. Simulation uses: rooftop PV hosting capacity and distributed generation scenarios. Related records: the NREL PV Rooftop Database and REPLICA.
